subject: machine-paced-delivery
seam: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:285 (`if (payload.stop_hook_active) process.exit(0)`) + the three-state exit contract at :248-266, wired via .claude/settings.json hooks.Stop
seam_note: This gate corrected the technique twice. It mutates nothing and BLOCKS nothing (its own header: 'Nothing here ever blocks') -- and it still guards re-entry, because exit 2 feeds a reminder to the model, the model acts, acting ends another turn, and the turn end re-fires the hook. So the termination contract is created by the gate's output RE-ENTERING THE AGENT'S LOOP, not by blocking and not by mutation; advisory is the weakest tier and the one most likely to ship unguarded. Technique redrafted twice mid-run to the three-tier form (advisory / blocking / mutating). Second corroboration: the hook's recorded history is the liveness paragraph made concrete -- it detected nothing for its entire life, replayed over all 31 transcripts, 1,136 Edit/Write calls, ZERO detections, because its turn-boundary scan stopped at the first user-role entry and 3,837 of 4,187 user-role entries are tool results. Ran green every turn and was indistinguishable from a working gate. Reached gate-liveness's three-state contract (0 pass / 2 model-actionable / 3 could-not-run) independently, after being burned by exactly that failure.
ship_reason: the gate already implements the technique's re-entry rule; nothing to change -- this is a confirming tree, read-only
return_condition: counters on the re-entry path and the could-not-run path, both currently unobservable: a gate that has never reported a skip and a gate whose skip path is broken look identical

seam_note: Two independent bounds on one loop, neither derived from the other. Falsifier RUN before the change, not argued: a scripted researcher that never shapes a report, max_turns=200, default chunk 8 -> stop_reason=step_cap, steps=12, num_turns=96. 104 requested turns were never spendable and no field said so, so raising max_turns past the ceiling was indistinguishable from raising it below one. subject: tool-result-economy
seam: crates/engine-claude/src/lib.rs:919-931 (envelope_text falls back to the raw `result` value, serialized, uncapped)
seam_note: Amendment landed this run: a bounding stage's failure path is correlated with the input it was bounding, so the involuntary fallback emits its largest payload where the transform was most needed - and it is invisible to the elected-recovery rate. Walked against three real sites in this tree and the amendment did NOT hold at two of them, which is the honest result. [remote] max_body_bytes and PARTIAL_CAP_CHARS (4000) both cap their fallbacks below the trigger, as the amendment prescribes. The third, MAX_SHIM_COMMAND_LINE at :800, states the amendment's disclosure rule in the tree's own words - ':838, a refusal is loud, a truncated command line is not' - and REFUSES rather than truncating, which is stronger than what the amendment asks for. Residue is one site: envelope_text's raw-result fallback is bounded only by what the CLI returned and carries no marker saying the payload is raw rather than structured.
ship_reason: two of three sites already satisfy the amendment independently; the third is one uncapped fallback whose blast radius is a CLI envelope, not a fetched page
return_condition: a counter separating involuntary fallbacks from elected ones - neither is instrumented anywhere, so a rising involuntary rate would be discovered during an incident

subject: fleet-orchestration
seam: none - crates/apps/research/src/lib.rs delegates the whole agentic loop to an external CLI
seam_note: The technique governs where a model-dispatcher's reasoning sits and whether it is durable. pumper does not own that placement: it hands a prompt to an agent CLI and receives text, so the deliberation happens inside a process whose transcript pumper never sees. Recording it would mean pumper parsing another tool's turn stream, which is a different subject. Not a rejection of the technique - the seam is in the CLI, not here.
return_condition: when a project runs its own dispatcher loop rather than shelling out to one, or when the engine surfaces the agent's per-turn transcript
